1	# Flow Editing Operations — Edit / Write Strategy
2	
3	All flow file modifications via the `Edit` and `Write` tools (read-modify-write of the `.flow` JSON file). This strategy gives full control over every field but requires manual management of definitions, variables, and edge integrity.
4	
5	> **Apply every recipe in this file with the `Edit` tool (default) or the `Write` tool (only when ≥70% of nodes change).** Each recipe shows the JSON payload that goes into the `new_string` parameter of an `Edit` call. `python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, and shell heredocs are a last resort for mutations and require explicit user approval after you've surfaced the trade-offs — see SKILL.md rule on scripted mutations and [editing-operations.md — Why not Python / Node / jq / sed?](editing-operations.md#why-not-python--node--jq--sed).
6	>
7	> **When to use this strategy:** Edit / Write is required for all non-carve-out `.flow` edits. Use Flow CLI only for connector activity, connector-trigger, and managed HTTP carve-outs documented by their plugins. Inline-agent project lifecycle uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow` / `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow` / `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow`, but the `uipath.agent.autonomous` node and edges are authored with this guide. See [editing-operations.md](editing-operations.md) for the strategy selection matrix.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Key Differences from CLI
12	
13	When editing the `.flow` file with `Edit` / `Write`, **you** are responsible for everything the CLI normally handles:
14	
15	| Concern | CLI handles | Edit / Write — you must |
16	|---------|------------|------------------------|
17	| Definitions | Auto-copied from registry cache | Copy the returned node definition object from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions` array |
18	| Node variables | Auto-added to `variables.nodes` | Add output variable entries manually (or accept that `variables.nodes` may need regeneration) |
19	| Edge cleanup on delete | Auto-removes connected edges | Find and remove all edges referencing the deleted node |
20	| Orphan cleanup | Auto-removes unused definitions and orphaned bindings | Remove definitions no longer referenced by any node; remove connector bindings only when no remaining node uses that connector |
21	| `targetPort` | Auto-set | Set `targetPort` on every edge (validate rejects without it) |
22	| `bindings_v2.json` | Auto-managed by `node configure` | Prefer the CLI carve-out for connector/managed HTTP configuration; if using the documented fallback, author top-level `.flow` `bindings[]` and only touch generated files when the plugin explicitly says to |
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Pre-flight Checklist
27	
28	Before editing the `.flow` file, ensure each of the following is handled. These are the concerns the CLI used to manage automatically; under the Edit / Write default, **you** are responsible for them.
29	
30	1. **Locate the canonical `.flow` file.** Before any `Edit` / `Write`, find the flow project directory — it is the directory that contains `project.uiproj`. The canonical `.flow` lives **next to** that `project.uiproj`, not at the solution root. Commands like `uip solution init <Name>` + `uip maestro flow init <Name>` create nested paths (`<Name>/<Name>/project.uiproj`); the `.flow` you must edit is `<Name>/<Name>/<Name>.flow`, not `<Name>/<Name>.flow`. Run `find . -name project.uiproj -type f` and pin every `Edit` / `Write` call to the sibling file. `uip maestro flow validate <PATH>.flow` will accept a misplaced file, so validation alone does **not** confirm the right target — only the colocation with `project.uiproj` does.
31	2. **Definitions and versions.** For every new node type, run `uip maestro flow registry get <type> --output json`. Copy the returned node definition object **verbatim** into `definitions[]` — one entry per unique `type:typeVersion`. Depending on CLI/plugin version, the node definition may appear as `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`; copy that node object, not the surrounding `Result` / `Code` envelope. Then set each node instance's `typeVersion` to match the copied definition's `version` exactly — string match, no normalization. Never hand-write or paraphrase definitions (see "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [the Author capability index](../CAPABILITY.md)). For node types with a documented `uip maestro flow node add` carve-out (managed HTTP, connector activities, connector triggers), use the CLI — see [http/impl.md — Step 1](plugins/http/impl.md#add-the-node).
32	3. **Unique node ID.** Pick a camelCase ID that does not collide with existing node IDs. Prefer meaningful names (`fetchUsers`, `filterActive`) since they become part of every `$vars.<nodeId>.*` expression.
33	4. **`sourcePort` and `targetPort` on every edge.** Omitting `targetPort` is the #1 validation error (see "`targetPort` is required on every edge" in [the Author capability index](../CAPABILITY.md)). Use `sourcePort`, never `sourceHandle`; `sourceHandle` is not part of the `.flow` edge schema and produces a precise schema error such as `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` (the path tells you exactly which edge entry is missing the `sourcePort` key). Look up ports in the relevant plugin's `planning.md` or in [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md). If an edge uses `sourcePort: "error"`, the source node must also have `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; `uip maestro flow format` self-heals this, but direct JSON edits must set it.
34	5. **Node outputs block (End / Terminate only).** End-style nodes consume their `outputs` block at runtime to map workflow-level `out` variables — see [end/impl.md](plugins/end/impl.md). For action / trigger nodes the instance `outputs` block is **not** consumed by BPMN serialization; the runtime reads the manifest's `outputDefinition` instead. Authoring an action-node `outputs` block matching the manifest is fine and is what the canonical examples show, but adding it does **not** make `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve downstream — that contract is `variables.nodes[]` (next item).
35	6. **`variables.nodes[]` (REQUIRED for every data-producing node — this is what powers `$vars.X.output`).** For each data-producing node, add an entry per output (`output` for action / trigger nodes, plus `error` for action nodes). The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; without them, downstream `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolves to `undefined` even though `flow validate` passes (MST-9972). The shape per entry: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`. After your edits, **`uip maestro flow format` regenerates this block from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** — running format makes any direct-authored omission self-healing.
36	7. **On delete — cascade manually.** Remove the node from `nodes`. Then sweep `edges[]` for any with matching `sourceNodeId`/`targetNodeId`. Then prune `definitions[]` if this was the last user of the type. Then check `bindings_v2.json` — but only remove a connector binding if no remaining node uses the same connector (bindings are shared at the connector level).
37	
38	> **Anti-pattern: editing a `.flow` that is not colocated with `project.uiproj`.**
39	> A `.flow` file outside the flow project directory is invisible to `uip maestro flow debug`, to the Studio solution, and to any checker that discovers the project via `**/project.uiproj`. It will still pass `uip maestro flow validate <PATH>.flow` because that command only checks JSON-schema correctness of the file you hand it — it does not verify the file is the project's canonical flow. Always edit the `.flow` that sits next to `project.uiproj`.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Edit Tooling
44	
45	Direct JSON edits use four mechanics. Pick by operation class — same pattern, different tool. The CLI has no `node update` command (see [editing-operations-cli.md § Operations Not Supported by CLI](editing-operations-cli.md#operations-not-supported-by-cli)), so structural mutations of node `inputs`, definition swaps, and array splices are done through direct `.flow` authoring.
46	
47	| Operation class | Mechanic | When to use |
48	|----|----|----|
49	| Surgical leaf-value change (single string/number/bool) | `Edit` | One unique substring in the file. Whitespace-sensitive — re-`Read` first if the file was just rewritten. |
50	| New node, new edge, new definition entry, new variable | `Read` whole file → reconstruct in chat → `Write` whole file | Adding self-contained sub-objects. Preserves field order; risks dropping fields on files >1000 lines. |
51	| Replace nested object in array; insert nested fields; idempotent splice | `Edit` / `Write`; `python3` heredoc only after explicit user approval | Surgical structural mutation. Prefer direct authoring first; use a script only when the user has accepted the state-bypass and diff-review trade-off. |
52	| One-shot extraction or single-field mutation from CLI JSON output | `jq` | Reading `--output json` results. Faster than spawning Python for read-only paths. |
53	
54	### Canonical heredoc recipe
55	
56	When the user explicitly approves a scripted structural rewrite, use this shape. Substitute the node-type guard, the field path, and the new value:
57	
58	```bash
59	python3 - <<'PY'
60	import json
61	flow = json.load(open("<FILE>.flow"))
62	# Mutate flow here — splice arrays, set nested fields, replace objects.
63	# Example: insert/overwrite a field on every node of a given type
64	for node in flow["nodes"]:
65	    if node.get("type") == "<NODE_TYPE>":
66	        node.setdefault("inputs", {})["<FIELD>"] = "<VALUE>"
67	json.dump(flow, open("<FILE>.flow", "w"), indent=2)
68	PY
69	uip maestro flow validate <FILE>.flow --output json
70	```
71	
72	`json.dump(..., indent=2)` matches the file's existing 2-space indent — `flow format` normalizes layout but does not re-indent unrelated structure, so preserve the canonical 2-space indent on writes.
73	
74	### `--output-filter` for extracting CLI JSON
75	
76	Read-only extractions on `--output json` results — use the CLI's built-in JMESPath filter, no external parser needed. Expressions start at the `Data` envelope (no `Data.` prefix). See [shared/cli-conventions.md §3](../../shared/cli-conventions.md#3-prefer---output-filter-for-extraction) for the full pattern.
77	
78	```bash
79	uip solution upload --output json --output-filter "Url"
80	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node"
81	```
82	
83	Reach for `jq` / `python3` only when JMESPath cannot express the operation (multi-step joins, format conversion, conditional output computed from multiple fields).
84	
85	### Why scripting is approval-gated
86	
87	- `Edit` on nested JSON is fragile. Indented sibling fields, trailing commas, and quote styles all break the exact-match constraint. One byte of drift, no edit applied.
88	- Whole-file `Write` is safe but lossy — every field has to round-trip through chat, and large `.flow` files (>500 lines once layout, definitions, and bindings settle) blow the read budget. Use `Write` only for new flows or full reshapes.
89	- `python3 -c` / heredoc is a fallback for structural rewrites that are too brittle for `Edit` and too large for safe whole-file `Write`. Use it only after surfacing the trade-offs and getting explicit user approval.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## Primitive Operations
94	
95	> **Multiple `Edit`s in one turn?** Several recipes below touch more than one top-level array at once (Add a node hits `nodes[]`, `definitions[]`, `variables.nodes`, and `layout.nodes`). Same-file `Edit`s serialize and must not share an anchor — anchor each on its target array's OWN opening key (never on top-level key order, which is not guaranteed) and watch for `"nodes": [` / `"edges": [` recurring inside `definitions[]` and `subflows.<id>`. Full rules: [editing-operations.md — Parallel same-file Edits](editing-operations.md#parallel-same-file-edits).
96	
97	### Add a node
98	
99	**Tool:** `Edit` (insert into `nodes[]` + `definitions[]` + `variables.nodes` + `layout.nodes`)
100	
101	1. Run `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json` and copy the returned node definition object (`Data.Node` or the top-level node object, depending on CLI/plugin version)
102	2. Use `Edit` to add a node entry to the `nodes` array:
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "id": "<UNIQUE_NODE_ID>",
107	  "type": "<NODE_TYPE>",
108	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
109	  "display": { "label": "<LABEL>" },
110	  "inputs": {},
111	  "outputs": {
112	    "output": {
113	      "type": "object",
114	      "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
115	      "source": "=result.response",
116	      "var": "output"
117	    },
118	    "error": {
119	      "type": "object",
120	      "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
121	      "source": "=result.Error",
122	      "var": "error"
123	    }
124	  }
125	}
126	```
127	
128	> **`display` is required on every node** — including control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`) where it may feel optional. Omitting it produces a vague `[(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined` from `uip maestro flow validate`, which does NOT pinpoint the missing field. Always include `"display": { "label": "<label>" }` on every node, even bare end nodes. See [file-format.md — Node instance](../../shared/file-format.md#node-instance).
129	
130	> **What actually makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve is `variables.nodes[]` (step 4 below), not the instance `outputs` block.** The BPMN emitter ignores the action-node instance `outputs` block at serialization — it reads the manifest's `outputDefinition` for the activity-side mapping and reads `variables.nodes[]` for the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations downstream nodes depend on. Authoring an `outputs` block matching the manifest is fine (the canonical examples include it for documentation), but you can skip it on action and trigger nodes. End / terminate nodes are different — see [end/impl.md](plugins/end/impl.md). The standard patterns are in [file-format.md — Node outputs](../../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from the current node graph (MST-9972).**
131	
132	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates are provided by the definition in `definitions[]` (copied verbatim from the registry). Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`/`isDefaultEntryPoint` for triggers, `color`/`content` for sticky notes, and `source` for every inline-agent-related node — `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) writes the inline agent's `projectId` (autonomous) or resource UUID (resource nodes) at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists source identity onto the instance — no `"model": { "source": ... }` block is written. See [file-format.md — Instance-specific identity fields](../../shared/file-format.md#instance-specific-identity-fields).
133	
134	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Do NOT put `position`, `size`, or `collapsed` on the node. Add a layout entry instead (step 5).
135	
136	3. Add the definition to `definitions` (if this type is not already present):
137	   - Paste the returned node definition object from the registry response
138	   - Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the pasted definition's exact `version`
139	   - One definition per unique `type:typeVersion` — not one per node instance
140	
141	> **Resource nodes — extra step.** If the node type is one of `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.agent.*`, `uipath.core.flow.*`, `uipath.core.agentic-process.*`, `uipath.core.api-workflow.*`, or `uipath.core.human-task.*`:
142	> 1. The instance stays minimal — just `inputs`/`outputs`/`display`.
143	> 2. Add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array (sibling of `nodes`/`edges`/`definitions`): two entries per resource (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` exactly matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
144	>
145	> The BPMN emit layer rewrites the definition's `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders to `=bindings.{id}` by matching on `(resourceKey, name)`. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." The definition stays verbatim from the registry — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside it. See the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for the exact JSON.
146	
147	4. Add node output variables to `variables.nodes` (REQUIRED — the BPMN emitter reads this to declare process-level variables. `uip maestro flow format` regenerates this block from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so running format after edits will self-heal an omitted entry; running validate alone does not. Without it, downstream `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolves to `undefined` at runtime — MST-9972):
148	
149	```json
150	[
151	  {
152	    "id": "<NODE_ID>.output",
153	    "type": "object",
154	    "description": "<Output description>",
155	    "binding": {
156	      "nodeId": "<NODE_ID>",
157	      "outputId": "output"
158	    }
159	  },
160	  {
161	    "id": "<NODE_ID>.error",
162	    "type": "object",
163	    "description": "Error information if the node fails",
164	    "binding": {
165	      "nodeId": "<NODE_ID>",
166	      "outputId": "error"
167	    }
168	  }
169	]
170	```
171	
172	5. Add a placeholder layout entry for the node in the top-level `layout.nodes` object — `flow format` rewrites both `position` and `size` on save:
173	
174	```json
175	"layout": {
176	  "nodes": {
177	    "<UNIQUE_NODE_ID>": {
178	      "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
179	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
180	      "collapsed": false
181	    }
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	**Layout rule:** Don't compute coordinates by hand — run `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` after edits. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's size by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows.
187	
188	### Delete a node
189	
190	**Tool:** `Edit` (remove from `nodes[]` + dependent edges + orphaned definitions + `variables.nodes` + `variableUpdates`)
191	
192	1. Use `Edit` to remove the node object from `nodes`
193	2. Remove **all edges** where `sourceNodeId` or `targetNodeId` equals the node's `id`
194	3. If no other node uses the same `type`, remove the definition from `definitions`
195	4. Remove the node's entry from `variables.nodes`
196	5. Remove any `variableUpdates` entries keyed by the node's `id`
197	6. If the node is a connector node, remove its binding from `bindings_v2.json` **only if no other node in the flow uses the same connector**. Bindings are shared at the connector level (keyed by `metadata.Connector`), not per node.
198	
199	### Add an edge
200	
201	**Tool:** `Edit` (insert into `edges[]` with `targetPort`)
202	
203	Use `Edit` to add an edge object to the `edges` array:
204	
205	```json
206	{
207	  "id": "edge_<SOURCE_NODE_ID>_<SOURCE_PORT>_<TARGET_NODE_ID>_<TARGET_PORT>",
208	  "sourceNodeId": "<SOURCE_NODE_ID>",
209	  "sourcePort": "<SOURCE_PORT>",
210	  "targetNodeId": "<TARGET_NODE_ID>",
211	  "targetPort": "<TARGET_PORT>"
212	}
213	```
214	
215	**Critical:** `targetPort` is required on every edge. Omitting it produces a validation error.
216	
217	**Critical:** the outgoing port field is named `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. `sourceHandle` is a UI/runtime term, not valid `.flow` JSON.
218	
219	**Critical:** for `sourcePort: "error"`, also set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node. Without the flag, Studio Web hides the source handle and `uip maestro flow validate` fails.
220	
221	**Edge ID:** `edge_<SOURCE_NODE_ID>_<SOURCE_PORT>_<TARGET_NODE_ID>_<TARGET_PORT>`.
222	
223	See each plugin's `planning.md` or [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md) for port names by node type.
224	
225	### Delete an edge
226	
227	**Tool:** `Edit`
228	
229	Use `Edit` to remove the edge object from the `edges` array by its `id`.
230	
231	### Update node inputs
232	
233	**Tool:** `Edit` (in-place value tweak — preserves node ID and `$vars`)
234	
235	Use `Edit` to modify the `inputs` object of the target node in-place. No need to delete and re-add.
236	
237	```json
238	{
239	  "id": "checkStatus",
240	  "type": "core.logic.decision",
241	  "inputs": {
242	    "expression": "$vars.fetchData.output.statusCode === 200"
243	  }
244	}
245	```
246	
247	This is a key advantage of `Edit` — input updates are a single field edit, not the delete + re-add pattern required by the CLI.
248	
249	---
250	
251	## Variable Operations
252	
253	These are `Edit`-only — the CLI does not support variable management. There is no fallback strategy.
254	
255	### Add a workflow variable
256	
257	**Tool:** `Edit`
258	
259	Use `Edit` to add an entry to `variables.globals`:
260	
261	```json
262	{
263	  "id": "<VARIABLE_ID>",
264	  "direction": "in|out|inout",
265	  "type": "string|number|boolean|object|array",
266	  "defaultValue": "<OPTIONAL_DEFAULT>",
267	  "description": "<OPTIONAL_DESCRIPTION>"
268	}
269	```
270	
271	For `out` variables: add output mapping to **every reachable End node** (see below).
272	For `inout` variables: add `variableUpdates` entries on nodes that modify the state.
273	
274	See [variables-and-expressions.md](../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the full schema, type system, and scoping rules.
275	
276	### Add output mapping on an End node
277	
278	**Tool:** `Edit`
279	
280	Use `Edit` to map every `out` variable in `variables.globals` on every reachable End node:
281	
282	```json
283	{
284	  "id": "doneSuccess",
285	  "type": "core.control.end",
286	  "typeVersion": "1.0.0",
287	  "display": { "label": "Done" },
288	  "inputs": {},
289	  "outputs": {
290	    "<VARIABLE_ID>": {
291	      "source": "=js:<EXPRESSION>"
292	    }
293	  }
294	}
295	```
296	
297	Each key in `outputs` must match a variable `id` from `variables.globals` where `direction: "out"`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
298	
299	### Add a variable update
300	
301	**Tool:** `Edit`
302	
303	Use `Edit` to add an entry to `variables.variableUpdates.<NODE_ID>`:
304	
305	```json
306	{
307	  "variables": {
308	    "variableUpdates": {
309	      "<NODE_ID>": [
310	        {
311	          "variableId": "<INOUT_VARIABLE_ID>",
312	          "expression": "=js:<EXPRESSION>"
313	        }
314	      ]
315	    }
316	  }
317	}
318	```
319	
320	Only `inout` variables can be updated. `in` variables are read-only.
321	
322	---
323	
324	## Composite Operations
325	
326	### Insert a node between two existing nodes
327	
328	**Tool:** `Edit` × 3 (delete old edge, add new node, add 2 new edges)
329	
330	1. Use `Edit` to remove the edge connecting the two nodes from the `edges` array
331	2. Use `Edit` to add the new node to `nodes` (with definition in `definitions`)
332	3. Use `Edit` to add two new edges:
333	   - upstream → new node (using upstream's output port → new node's `input`)
334	   - new node → downstream (using new node's output port → downstream's `input`)
335	
336	### Insert a decision branch
337	
338	**Tool:** `Edit` × 3 (delete old edge, add decision node, add 3 new edges)
339	
340	1. Use `Edit` to remove the edge where the branch should go
341	2. Use `Edit` to add the decision node to `nodes` with `inputs.expression`
342	3. Use `Edit` to add three edges:
343	   - upstream → decision (target port: `input`)
344	   - decision → true branch (source port: `true`, target port: `input`)
345	   - decision → false branch (source port: `false`, target port: `input`)
346	
347	### Remove a node and reconnect
348	
349	**Tool:** `Edit` × 4 (delete node, sweep edges, prune orphan definitions, add reconnect edge)
350	
351	1. Record the node's upstream and downstream connections from `edges`
352	2. Use `Edit` to remove the node from `nodes`
353	3. Use `Edit` to remove all edges referencing the node
354	4. Use `Edit` to clean up orphaned definitions
355	5. Use `Edit` to add a new edge connecting upstream directly to downstream
356	
357	### Replace a mock with a real resource node
358	
359	**Tool:** `Edit` (multiple calls — replace node, edges, definitions, bindings, variables)
360	
361	1. Get the resource node manifest — check in-solution first, then tenant registry:
362	   ```bash
363	   # In-solution (preferred — no login required):
364	   uip maestro flow registry get "<RESOURCE_NODE_TYPE>" --local --output json
365	
366	   # Tenant registry (if not in solution):
367	   uip maestro flow registry get "<RESOURCE_NODE_TYPE>" --output json
368	   ```
369	2. Record the mock node's connected edges
370	3. Remove the mock node from `nodes`
371	4. Remove all edges referencing the mock
372	5. Add the real resource node to `nodes` with:
373	   - Correct `type` and `typeVersion`
374	   - `inputs` with resolved field values
375	   - `outputs` block (action nodes: `output` + `error`)
376	   - No `model` block — binding/context templates come from the definition
377	6. Copy the definition from registry into `definitions`
378	7. Add entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array — two per resource (`name` + `folderPath`), with `resourceKey` matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`
379	8. Re-create all edges using the new node's `id`
380	9. Add node variables to `variables.nodes`
381	10. Validate: `uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json`
382	
383	### Replace manual trigger with scheduled trigger
384	
385	**Tool:** `Edit` × 2 (start node in-place, swap definition)
386	
387	Use `Edit` to modify the start node in-place (no delete/re-add needed):
388	
389	1. Change `type` from `core.trigger.manual` to `core.trigger.scheduled`
390	2. Add timer inputs (keep the existing `entryPointId` in `inputs`):
391	   ```json
392	   "inputs": {
393	     "entryPointId": "<existing-uuid>",
394	     "timerType": "timeCycle",
395	     "timerPreset": "R/PT1H"
396	   }
397	   ```
398	3. Update the definition in `definitions`:
399	   - Remove the `core.trigger.manual` definition
400	   - Add the `core.trigger.scheduled` definition from `uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.scheduled --output json` (the new definition carries the correct `model.type` and `model.eventDefinition`)
401	4. Validate: `uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json`
402	
403	### Create a subflow
404	
405	**Tool:** `Edit` (or `Write` if scaffolding from template)
406	
407	1. Use `Edit` to add a `core.subflow` parent node to `nodes`:
408	   ```json
409	   {
410	     "id": "<SUBFLOW_NODE_ID>",
411	     "type": "core.subflow",
412	     "typeVersion": "1.0.0",
413	     "display": { "label": "<LABEL>" },
414	     "inputs": {
415	       "<IN_VAR>": "=js:<EXPRESSION>"
416	     },
417	     "outputs": {
418	       "output": {
419	         "type": "object",
420	         "description": "The return value of the subflow",
421	         "source": "=result.response",
422	         "var": "output"
423	       },
424	       "error": {
425	         "type": "object",
426	         "description": "Error information if the subflow fails",
427	         "source": "=result.Error",
428	         "var": "error"
429	       }
430	     }
431	   }
432	   ```
433	
434	2. Use `Edit` to add a `subflows.<SUBFLOW_NODE_ID>` entry with its own nodes, edges, variables, and layout:
435	   ```json
436	   {
437	     "subflows": {
438	       "<SUBFLOW_NODE_ID>": {
439	         "nodes": [
440	           { "id": "sfStart", "type": "core.trigger.manual", ... },
441	           { "id": "sfEnd", "type": "core.control.end", ... }
442	         ],
443	         "edges": [ ... ],
444	         "variables": {
445	           "globals": [
446	             { "id": "<IN_VAR>", "direction": "in", "type": "..." },
447	             { "id": "<OUT_VAR>", "direction": "out", "type": "..." }
448	           ],
449	           "nodes": []
450	         },
451	         "layout": {
452	           "nodes": {
453	             "sfStart": { "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 }, "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 }, "collapsed": false },
454	             "sfEnd":   { "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 }, "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 }, "collapsed": false }
455	           }
456	         }
457	       }
458	     }
459	   }
460	   ```
461	
462	3. Subflow's `in` variables must match the parent node's `inputs` keys
463	4. Map all `out` variables on the subflow's End node `outputs`
464	5. Parent-scope `$vars` are NOT visible inside the subflow — pass values via inputs
465	6. Subflow node positions go in the **subflow's own** `layout.nodes` — not in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Each subflow has an independent layout scope.
466	
467	See [subflow/impl.md](plugins/subflow/impl.md) for the full JSON structure and rules.
468	
469	---
470	
471	## Connector Node Configuration (Edit / Write fallback)
472	
473	When not using `uip maestro flow node configure`, use `Edit` to set up the following manually:
474	
475	### 1. `inputs.detail` on the node
476	
477	**Tool:** `Edit`
478	
479	```json
480	{
481	  "inputs": {
482	    "detail": {
483	      "connectionId": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
484	      "folderKey": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
485	      "method": "<HTTP_METHOD>",
486	      "endpoint": "<API_PATH>",
487	      "bodyParameters": { "<FIELD>": "<VALUE>" },
488	      "queryParameters": { "<FIELD>": "<VALUE>" },
489	      "pathParameters": { "<PLACEHOLDER>": "<VALUE>" }
490	    }
491	  }
492	}
493	```
494	
495	Source `method`, `endpoint`, and `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` field names from either of these (both read the same upstream IS metadata):
496	
497	From `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --connection-id <id> --output json`:
498	- `method` ← `connectorMethodInfo.method`
499	- `endpoint` ← `connectorMethodInfo.path`
500	- `bodyParameters.<name>` ← `inputDefinition.fields[].name`
501	- `queryParameters.<name>` ← `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: query`
502	- `pathParameters.<name>` ← `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: path` (must match a `{placeholder}` in `endpoint`)
503	
504	From `uip is resources describe <connector-key> <objectName> --connection-id <id> --operation <Op> --output json`:
505	- `method` ← `availableOperations[].method`
506	- `endpoint` ← `availableOperations[].path`
507	- `bodyParameters.<name>` ← `requestFields[].name`
508	- `queryParameters.<name>` ← `parameters[]` where `type: query`
509	- `pathParameters.<name>` ← `parameters[]` where `type: path` (must match a `{placeholder}` in `endpoint`)
510	
511	### 2. Connection binding in `bindings_v2.json`
512	
513	**Tool:** `Edit` (or `Write` for a fresh `bindings_v2.json`)
514	
515	```json
516	{
517	  "version": "2.0",
518	  "resources": [
519	    {
520	      "resource": "Connection",
521	      "key": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
522	      "id": "Connection<CONNECTION_UUID>",
523	      "value": {
524	        "ConnectionId": {
525	          "defaultValue": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
526	          "isExpression": false,
527	          "displayName": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"
528	        }
529	      },
530	      "metadata": {
531	        "ActivityName": "<ACTIVITY_DISPLAY_NAME>",
532	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
533	        "DisplayLabel": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
534	        "UseConnectionService": "true",
535	        "Connector": "<CONNECTOR_KEY>"
536	      }
537	    }
538	  ]
539	}
540	```
541	
542	See [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md) for the full schema and multi-connector examples.
